We ran the forecast with our infra team and two questions came up we hoped you could confirm before we share with procurement: 1) If we take the Modular Uplift (adds low-latency RealTime API + 30k throughput), is there a one-time migration credit for unused Compact credits? 2) Alternatively, can we do a credit-swap where unused Compact/Compact+ credits convert at a 0.6x rate toward the Uplift pack instead of paying upfront?

Ava suggested sharing the usage snapshot — attaching. We need the economics nailed down by next Tuesday to keep our quarter procurement cadence.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Jordan — thanks for the clear ask and the snapshot. Quick answers upfront: 1) One-time migration credit: yes, we offer a prorated migration credit for committed annual contracts when moving from Compact families into Dedicated/Uplift packs — typically calculated on remaining unused committed tokens. 2) Credit-swap program: we can do a swap but at a discount factor — our standard internal guideline is 0.6x for usage credits (Compact -> Uplift) unless you also take the Observability retention addon and a 12-month commit, in which case we can push to 0.75x.

I'll loop Ben to run the exact numbers against your attached snapshot, and Marcus to model the SLA/routing implications for RealTime. If it's helpful, I can send a short pro-forma with both scenarios (credit-swap vs. uplift upfront) showing monthly cashflow and per-token unit economics.

Next steps: Ben, Marcus — can you run the swap model + uplift amortization and draft a pro-forma by EOD Monday? Jordan/Ava — if you have procurement constraints (e.g., cannot accept credits with more than 6-month vesting), flag them.

Irene Choi
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

Jordan / team — I ran two quick scenarios against the snapshot:

- Scenario A (Upfront Uplift): One-year Uplift pack (includes Realtime) at list $120k/yr. We apply a prorated migration credit for remaining Compact committed spend (from your usage file) — that credit reduces cash due at signing by ~ $18.3k. Effective first-year net is $101.7k.

- Scenario B (Credit-swap): Convert remaining Compact credits at 0.6x into Uplift token equivalents. That yields a swap value equal to $11.0k of Uplift consumption. To cover observed throughput gap and the RealTime provision, you'd pay the delta as a top-up of $35k and sign a 12-month term. Total first-year outflow ~ $46k, but note this leaves you on a metered overlay with higher marginals after swap exhaustion.

If Clearline prefers higher conversion, we can do 0.75x if you take: (a) 12-month commit and (b) Observability retention addon (90d) at a 15% bundled discount. That blended option lands at ~$67k first-year net with RealTime included.

Marcus — any sharp notes on latency/backfill costs we should call out if Jordan expects immediate parity with Dedicated?

Ben
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Modular pack uplift vs. credit-swap — need clarity

Jordan — short technical note on the RealTime add-on: the Uplift pack provisions a reserved pool with faster scheduling and KV-prefetch prioritization. If you do a pure credit-swap (Scenario B) we can enable RealTime but there are two trade-offs to call out:

1) Warmup: If your traffic pattern is bursty (your snapshot shows a diurnal spike), the reserved pool will need up to 48–72 hours to warm to peak efficiency without sustained baseline. That affects observed p99 latency for the first week.

2) Backfill & KV cache: We can preserve prefix cache if you agree to a 30-day overlap period where Compact traffic is routed through the same region; otherwise, the cache miss rate increases and your token cost per request rises ~8–12%.

Operationally: the 0.75x swap + Observability addon is the cleanest parity path — it gives you immediate throughput guarantees, longer retention for diffs, and reduces our risk of needing emergency capacity bursts. If Clearline needs the absolute lowest cash at sig, the pure swap (Scenario B) is lower cash but operationally heavier in the short term.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to walk ops through tuning and a migration runbook.

— Marcus Lin
APAC Infra & Reliability (serving runtime) — Redwood Inference
